title: Federal Rule 42 — consolidation and separate trials
shortTitle: Federal Rule 42 — consolidation and separate trials
summary: A court can coordinate related litigation or separate issues for trial without treating every procedural unit as one merged claim. These management choices seek efficiency while limiting prejudice and confusion.

sections.Role in the course: A court can coordinate related litigation or separate issues for trial without treating every procedural unit as one merged claim. These management choices seek efficiency while limiting prejudice and confusion.
sections.What to examine: Distinguish joining parties and claims in one action, consolidating separate actions, ordering separate trials of issues, and multidistrict coordination. Identify the rule or statute and the effect on party rights and judgments.
